questions.question: In his critique of rule utilitarianism, J. J. C. Smart famously argued that a rule utilitarian's refusal to break a general rule, even when doing so would maximize net happiness in a specific instance, leaves the position vulnerable to which conceptual charge?
options: The fallacy of composition
Irresponsible 'rule worship'
Infinite regress of moral duties
The naturalistic fallacy

questions.question: In classical virtue ethics, the thesis known as the 'Unity of the Virtues' asserts that:
options: An individual cannot fully possess any single moral virtue without possessing practical wisdom (phronesis) and all other moral virtues.
Every moral virtue can be reduced to and derived from a single fundamental duty of benevolence.
Moral virtues are functionally identical across all cultures regardless of historical or social context.
Virtuous conduct is entirely separable from internal dispositions and depends exclusively on consequences.

questions.question: In Donald Davidson's influential account of akrasia (weakness of will), how is it possible for an agent to act intentionally against their own better judgment without being entirely irrational?
options: The agent acts on a sub-personal, purely biological reflex that bypasses belief-desire mental states.
The agent mistakenly believes that their chosen action obeys a Kantian categorical imperative.
The agent holds an all-things-considered judgment favoring action A, yet acts intentionally on an unconditional judgment favoring action B.
The agent lacks the cognitive capacity to form conditional judgments regarding future outcomes.

questions.question: In contemporary philosophy of mind, David Chalmers uses the conceivability of 'philosophical zombies' (p-zombies) primarily to argue against which metaphysical thesis?
options: Property dualism
Epiphenomenalism
Substance dualism
Physicalism

questions.question: According to the logical positivists' Verification Principle (e.g., A. J. Ayer), a synthetic declarative sentence is cognitively meaningful if and only if it satisfies which condition?
options: It can be derived logically from self-evident rational axioms without empirical input.
It is capable of being empirically verified, at least in principle, through sensory observation.
It enhances the emotional solidarity and practical cohesion of a linguistic community.
It expresses an irreducible metaphysical truth regarding the fundamental nature of being.
